# Independent audit: same-separator power flattening and two entropies

Audited `candidate 0a0ac9e7c499601f`
in full. **PASS**, within its regular singleton, unpenalized, same-eta
physical-response scope. It does not assert actual-depth ascent or neutrality.

The original-volume reweighting is exact: with source mass sigma_i/L_i,
row probability rho_i, and bar rho_i=(L/L_i)rho_i, the L-tight row equation
makes bar rho_i a probability and sum sigma_i bar rho_i=dm/M. Consequently
the KL sum is exactly -sum sigma_i log L_i. The density ratio is bounded
away from zero and infinity; zero entropy forces pointwise preservation
of L on every positive volume row, not just its Jensen equality.

The raw path L^(1-t) is concave, positive, and already logarithmically
normalized on the fixed body. Its derivative is -L log L. For the stated
radial feasible-cone verification, take C at least 1+log of the maximum
of L on a fixed compact positive NEIGHBORHOOD, or strictly larger than
the corresponding old-body value; then Cs-s log s is increasing concave
on that whole range. This is only a neighborhood-choice clarification:
the exact power path independently establishes feasibility. The globally
finite convex tangent extension of -kappa log L is an allowed signed
complete-cut field. Keeping raw power and renormalizing on the actual
moving body adds precisely the already retained shape-log term, with
no missing extra first-order contribution.

The common response signs check directly:

    R_parameter = (1/N) sum e_i log L_i = -Delta K_V/N,
    R_body = integral Xi(-kappa log L) = -R_surface.

Thus the same-eta covering response is -(R_surface+Delta K_V/N).
The two nonnegative quantities add. The assertion is about selected
covering responses; a weighted upper-cover derivative does not identify
the derivative of the true maximum depth.

The conditional zero-response conclusion is valid. Positive volume rows
are absolutely continuous in every sampled fiber, so a nonzero continuous
gradient together with a fixed affine-contact level would confine such
a row to a fiberwise null hyperplane. All positive gradients must vanish,
and finite-PL continuity then makes L constant on each fiber. This does
not make it constant over different bases. The separate surface entropy
inequality independently forces its own rows to preserve L levels; no
identification of the two couplings is used.

Finally, reversal is genuinely unavailable for every nonconstant finite-PL
L: on a relative-open affine cell with nonzero gradient, L log L has
strictly positive second derivative along a varying segment. Adding any
multiple of the old affine L cannot make it concave. The old zero Jensen
gap on that segment also rules out a uniform first-order approximation
by feasible reversed paths, including sufficiently small body changes
that retain the segment. No missing two-sided stationarity can therefore
turn the displayed one-sided cost into a cancellation.
